name: Farm with a shop
description: A farm that sells its produce: the products with an enquiry basket, a price list and events such as harvest days or markets, with facts about the land, the produce, certification and deliveries.

questions.question: Since which year has your family or company been farming here?
How many hectares do you farm?
What do you grow, raise or make?
questions.help: A short list, e.g. "apples, cider, eggs, lamb".

questions.question: Is the farm certified organic? By whom and under which number?
questions.help: Only if you hold a valid certificate – the word organic is protected in many countries. Leave it empty otherwise.

questions.question: Do you deliver? Where to?
questions.help: For example "within 30 km every Friday" or "collection at the farm only".

questions.question: Can visitors pick their own? What and when?
questions.help: Leave it empty if you do not offer it.

audit.message: Say what you grow and produce – visitors decide in seconds whether the farm has what they want.
Add your produce as products so that customers can ask for it.
The products have not changed for half a year – produce is seasonal, check what is available now.
No event has been added for three months – add the next market, harvest day or open day.
Add the farm shop opening hours in Business details – nobody drives out to a closed gate.
Mark the farm on the map in Business details – farms are hard to find without it.

claude: Visitors of a farm site want to know what is on sale right now, when the shop is open, where the farm is and whether it delivers – put the current produce, the opening hours and the map first, and keep the opening hours in the settings so the site can say whether the shop is open. Write warmly but concretely, about real fields, animals and seasons, without idyllic cliches. Never call anything organic, local, free-range or award-winning unless the owner confirms a certificate or a fact behind it – such labels are regulated in many countries – and never invent harvest figures, animal numbers, prices or customer quotes. Produce is seasonal: mark availability on each product and prefer the facts and the products over text that will be wrong next month. Events (markets, harvest days, open days) go into the events collection so that past ones archive themselves.
